Using rigatoni, heavy cream, goat cheese, fresh rosemary, and shredded rotisserie chicken, Michael walks Clinton Kelly and Carla Hall through the deceptively simple recipe while sharing stories from his early days as a 22-year-old executive chef running a packed live-fire kitchen. The conversation turns nostalgic as Michael explains how the dish followed him from restaurant to restaurant and became such a customer favorite that he eventually had to remove it from the menu. The hosts laugh over Michael’s son Kyle unknowingly eating goat cheese for years despite insisting he hated it, while Clinton passionately defends rosemary after recalling a social media argument about the herb. The episode also features sponsor shout-outs to Fresh Direct and Frontgate, plus playful banter about portion sizes, “fat soup diets,” and airplane etiquette after eating rich pasta dishes. Once plated, the hosts rave about the comforting flavors, especially how the chicken melts into the creamy sauce and how the rosemary balances the tanginess of the goat cheese. The episode wraps with the selection of Melicia from New York as the “Fan of the Day,” followed by more joking between the hosts as they finish off the rich and nostalgic dish.

programme.title: Chewed Up

As he assembles a simple sesame-lime vinaigrette and tosses together cabbage, carrots, bok choy, bell peppers, scallions, and shredded chicken, the hosts discuss the value of leftovers, pantry staples, and the difference between a salad and simply a bowl of lettuce. Michael Symon shares thoughts on menu development and simple comfort foods like peanut butter and jelly sandwiches. The conversation evolves into a broader discussion about healthy eating habits, meal planning, and the realization that not every meal needs to be an indulgent experience. Along the way, the hosts joke about Clinton’s “Gay Soup Diet,” debate the merits of themed ingredient weeks, and exchange playful banter about fashion makeovers, aging, and personal style. Sponsor shout-outs to FreshDirect and Frontgate are woven into the episode, highlighting convenient grocery delivery and entertaining essentials. A fan mail segment sparks more comedy, including the possibility of a future Gay Soup Diet cookbook. The episode wraps with the hosts sampling the finished salad, celebrating its fresh flavors and nutritional balance, before signing off with thanks to viewers and listeners.

programme.title: Why'd They Wear That?
programme.desc: Clinton Kelly and Stacy London break down the iconic costumes in "When Harry Met Sally," designed by Gloria Gresham. The hosts trace fashion evolution across the film's 12-year timeline, from 1977 collegiate casual wear through early-80s yuppie aesthetics to late-80s power dressing and evening wear. They discuss standout pieces including Sally's navy knee-highs with shorts, the infamous oversized plaid sweater from the orgasm scene, off-shoulder dresses, and bridesmaid gowns. The analysis balances appreciation for authentic period styling with candid critiques of questionable fit and silhouette choices, ultimately celebrating how the costumes authentically capture the era without overshadowing the film's acclaimed dialogue.

programme.desc: 2019 marked the 50th anniversary of the Apollo 11 lunar landing. This incredible milestone changed the way humanity looked at our planet and access to deep space. programme.desc: The Beechcraft Company has been in existence for more than 88 years and has built some of the most influential aircraft in history. If you are lucky, you may even get a ride in CSPs souped-up Beechcraft King Air.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: Wildfires are growing in intensity, and firefighting aviation is becoming increasingly crucial to saving forests and lives in Colorado and beyond. Fire aviation teams are critical, complex efforts, made up of pilots, technicians, and coordinators who work together with ground crews to put out and contain wildfires. As environmental conditions set the stage for unprecedented fire seasons, night vision goggle technology is employed for the first time, and Colorado legislatures are paying closer attention than ever to the importance of wildfires. The progress is clear, yet so much remains to be done.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: New fire conditions call for new firefighting methods and tools. Looking at Calfire, we learn how the largest municipal fleet of firefighting aircraft in the world has developed over time. Live data feeds revolutionize how firefighting teams understand fires and communicate during missions. Colorado gets ready to purchase its first Firehawk helicopter, and interagency teams coordinate at the local, state, and federal levels. The challenges in fighting wildfires are greater than ever, but with new methods of fighting the fires, so are the opportunities.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: In the 1950s, The Century Series defined an era of aviation during the Cold War, charting a metamorphosis from one era to another. Jets were in their infancy, and many milestones, including the sound barrier, loomed large. In an arms race with the Soviet Union, a rising superpower, the U.S. got to work developing a variety of impressive fighter jets, now known as the Century Series. Starting with the F-100, the first production airplane to break the sound barrier in level flight, we explore how the century series pioneered new airplane designs, including the aerodynamic coke bottle shape made famous by the F-102. The F-104, a missile with a man in it inspired a generation of pilots. The F-105 looked like a fighter but was a bomber in disguise. As a series, their legacy is evident in modern fighter jets.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: For nearly sixty years the Learjet came to define a new class of luxury airplane the business jet. Now, the last Learjet ever is being assembled at the Wichita-based production facility in The Aviation Capital of the World. Speaking with aviation icons past and present, we get an intimate look at a company that shaped aviation as we know it today. From its record-setting performance achievements to its outsized role in popular culture, the Learjets place in history is here to stay, long after the production lines shut down.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: Early Space Exploration was defined by a Space race between the United States and the Soviet Union in a quest for national bragging rights. Major milestones like the first artificial Earth satellite, landing on the moon, and eventually creating the International Space Station (ISS) in 1993. Astronauts experience a psychological sensation called The Overview Effect. The ISS marked a new focus on international collaboration in Space. On the ISS, scientists are conducting novel research that is revolutionizing our understanding of life on earth -- from monitoring air pollution to fermenting beer. With the ISS expected to shut down in the coming decades, private space stations may play a larger role in the future of space- and exploration.
